system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Venice, . Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Venice itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Venice space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (San Marco, Dorsoduro, Cannaregio, Castello, Giudecca) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Venice spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Venice, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Victoria Miro Venice
galleries.address_hint: Calle Drio la Chiesa, San Marco 1994
galleries.note: The Venetian branch of an internationally prominent gallery, bringing major represented artists and a blue-chip programme to a permanent, seasonally operated space.

galleries.name: Palazzo Diedo – Berggruen Arts & Culture
galleries.note: An ambitious new cultural hub commissioning major site-specific works from internationally recognized contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Galerie Alberta Pane
galleries.note: A leading Venice–Paris gallery with a rigorous international programme, strong institutional links and regular art-fair participation.

galleries.name: Galleria Michela Rizzo
galleries.note: One of Venice’s most respected contemporary galleries, known for conceptually oriented artists and sustained institutional visibility.

galleries.name: Marignana Arte
galleries.note: A highly regarded programme combining established and emerging Italian and international artists, supported by fairs and museum collaborations.

galleries.name: Ocean Space
galleries.address_hint: Chiesa di San Lorenzo, Campo San Lorenzo
galleries.note: TBA21–Academy’s influential platform for ambitious art, ecology and ocean-focused commissions in the monumental Church of San Lorenzo.

galleries.name: A plus A Gallery
galleries.note: A long-running experimental gallery that has helped launch emerging practices while connecting exhibitions with curatorial research and education.

galleries.name: V–A–C Zattere
galleries.address_hint: Fondamenta Zattere al Ponte Longo, Dorsoduro 1401
galleries.note: The Venetian venue of V–A–C Foundation, notable for large-scale, research-led exhibitions and international institutional partnerships.

galleries.name: Caterina Tognon
galleries.note: An internationally recognized specialist in contemporary art using glass, with an influential programme extending well beyond traditional Murano practice.

galleries.name: Fondazione Bevilacqua La Masa
galleries.note: A historic Venetian institution whose exhibitions, studios and annual young-artists programme have shaped generations of local contemporary practice.

galleries.name: Fondazione Emilio e Annabianca Vedova
galleries.note: Preserves Vedova’s legacy while mounting serious exhibitions and cross-generational dialogues in spaces designed with Renzo Piano.

galleries.name: Patricia Low Venezia
galleries.note: The Venetian branch of the established Gstaad gallery presents internationally collected contemporary artists in a historic palazzo.

galleries.name: Tommaso Calabro Venezia
galleries.address_hint: Palazzo Donà Brusa, Campo San Polo
galleries.note: An influential Milan–Venice gallery combining postwar rediscoveries, artist estates and carefully selected contemporary positions.

galleries.name: Capsule Venice
galleries.note: A young nonprofit platform with an internationally oriented programme of emerging and mid-career artists, residencies and commissioned exhibitions.

galleries.name: SMAC – San Marco Art Centre
galleries.note: A major new exhibition centre whose scale, central location and interdisciplinary international programme give it immediate institutional importance.

galleries.name: Espace Louis Vuitton Venezia
galleries.note: A compact but prominent corporate cultural venue presenting commissioned projects and exhibitions connected with the Fondation Louis Vuitton collection.

galleries.name: Berengo Studio and Fondazione Berengo Art Space
galleries.note: A crucial bridge between contemporary art and Murano glass, internationally influential through artist collaborations and the recurring Glasstress project.

galleries.name: The Pool NYC at Palazzo Cesari Marchesi
galleries.note: An international gallery platform staging ambitious exhibitions in a permanent Venetian palazzo, often around the Biennale calendar.

galleries.name: Zuecca Projects
galleries.note: A well-established Venetian producer and exhibition platform responsible for numerous international contemporary-art projects across the city.

galleries.name: Ikona Gallery
galleries.note: Founded by Živa Kraus, this pioneering photography and contemporary-art gallery has sustained an independent programme since the late 1970s.

galleries.name: Spazio Punch
galleries.note: An agile nonprofit space supporting experimental exhibitions, publishing, design and interdisciplinary projects in a former industrial setting.

galleries.name: S.a.L.E. Docks
galleries.note: An artist-run and activist cultural space influential for politically engaged art, commons-based organization and critical debate around the Biennale.

galleries.name: Galleria d'Arte Maggiore g.a.m. Venezia
galleries.note: The Venice branch of a longstanding Italian gallery dealing in important modern masters alongside established contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Contini Art Gallery
galleries.address_hint: Calle Larga XXII Marzo, San Marco 2288
galleries.note: A longstanding commercial gallery with multiple Venetian premises, a recognizable roster and an international clientele for modern and contemporary art.

galleries.name: AKKA Project Venice
galleries.note: An internationally connected gallery distinguished in Venice by its sustained focus on contemporary artists from Africa and its diaspora.

galleries.name: European Cultural Centre – Italy
galleries.note: A large international exhibition platform operating Palazzo Mora, Palazzo Bembo and outdoor sites, especially visible during Biennale seasons.

galleries.name: Spazio Berlendis
galleries.note: A restored former workshop and chapel used for substantial contemporary exhibitions, installations and cultural projects.

galleries.name: Studio Cannaregio
galleries.note: An independent space known for focused presentations by emerging international artists and collaborations with galleries and curators.

galleries.name: CREA Cantieri del Contemporaneo
galleries.note: A multidisciplinary cultural centre providing production and exhibition space for independent art, performance and community-led projects.

galleries.name: Spazio Thetis
galleries.note: An unusual Arsenale venue and sculpture garden with a long record of hosting contemporary installations and Biennale-adjacent projects.

galleries.name: Castello 925
galleries.note: An independent exhibition and residency venue providing sustained visibility for emerging and mid-career international artists.

galleries.name: Giudecca 795 Art Gallery
galleries.note: A durable independent gallery presenting contemporary art, photography and projects attentive to Venice’s social and architectural context.

galleries.name: Beatrice Burati Anderson Art Space & Gallery
galleries.note: A curator-led space supporting interdisciplinary and socially attentive contemporary practices through exhibitions and special projects.

galleries.name: Bugno Art Gallery
galleries.note: A longstanding commercial gallery with a dependable programme of Italian and international modern and contemporary artists.

galleries.name: SPARC* – Spazio Arte Contemporanea
galleries.note: A centrally located independent venue presenting rotating exhibitions by contemporary Italian and international artists.

galleries.name: lineadacqua Gallery
galleries.note: A gallery and publishing initiative valued for researched exhibitions on Venetian visual culture, photography and modern or contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Deodato Arte Venezia
galleries.note: The Venetian outpost of a national gallery network specializing in accessible blue-chip, street, pop and contemporary art.

galleries.name: Bel-Air Fine Art Venice
galleries.note: Part of an international commercial network with a highly visible Venice presence and a broad programme of postwar, pop and contemporary work.

galleries.name: The Merchant House
galleries.note: A distinctive curatorial gallery crossing contemporary art, sculpture, design and artist-made jewelry, with carefully researched thematic exhibitions.

galleries.name: Galleria Ravagnan
galleries.note: A prominent family-run gallery active since the 1960s, maintaining a highly visible programme of modern and contemporary art.

galleries.name: Fondation Valmont at Palazzo Bonvicini
galleries.note: A corporate art foundation presenting recurring contemporary exhibitions and commissioned installations in a dedicated Venetian palazzo.

galleries.name: Fondation Wilmotte Gallery
galleries.note: A permanent foundation venue supporting contemporary architecture, design and art exhibitions, including work by emerging practitioners.

galleries.name: Arte Spazio Tempo
galleries.note: An established Ghetto-area gallery offering a steady programme of contemporary painting, sculpture, photography and international group exhibitions.

galleries.name: Visioni Altre
galleries.note: An independent gallery especially attentive to photography, installation and cross-cultural contemporary projects.

galleries.name: Galleria La Salizada
galleries.note: A longstanding independent gallery supporting Venetian and Italian contemporary artists through regularly changing exhibitions.

galleries.name: Galleria d'Arte L'Occhio
galleries.note: A durable small gallery near the Salute known for modern and contemporary works by Italian, Venetian and international artists.

galleries.name: Galleria S. Eufemia
galleries.note: A community-oriented Giudecca gallery providing public exhibition space for contemporary Venetian and visiting artists.

galleries.name: Casa Punto Croce
galleries.note: An intimate residency and exhibition initiative supporting artist-led experimentation and projects developed specifically in Venice.

galleries.name: Ca' Foscari Esposizioni
galleries.note: The university’s public exhibition programme has presented substantial international contemporary-art projects, particularly during Biennale periods.

galleries.name: Venice Projects
galleries.note: A specialist platform commissioning and exhibiting contemporary artists who engage experimentally with glass and Venetian craft production.

galleries.name: Luigi Proietti Gallery
galleries.note: A commercial gallery notable for bringing contemporary glass, sculpture and collectible art into dialogue with Venice’s material traditions.

galleries.name: Micromega Arte e Cultura
galleries.note: A small, longstanding gallery recognized for editions, optical and kinetic work, and carefully selected modern and contemporary artists.

galleries.name: THE ROOM Contemporary Art Space
galleries.note: ITS LIQUID’s permanent presentation space hosts frequent open-call and internationally sourced exhibitions across art, architecture and design.

galleries.name: San Polo Art Gallery
galleries.note: A centrally placed independent gallery with decades of activity in modern, contemporary and glass-related art.

galleries.name: Galleria d'Arte Santo Stefano
galleries.note: A longstanding local gallery maintaining a public programme of Italian figurative and contemporary art in a prominent cultural district.

galleries.name: Galleria d'Arte San Vidal
galleries.note: A historic artists’ association and exhibition venue that continues to provide public visibility for contemporary practitioners in Venice.
